# Tests that are expected to FAIL, one fully-qualified name per line.
#
# This file is a gate in both directions. .github/scripts/assert-baseline.py fails
# the build if a test outside this list fails, and equally if a test named here
# starts passing — a stale entry is itself a failure, the same rule
# tests/DbParity.Tests/policy/known-schema-divergences.txt lives by.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Both entries below reduce to one structural difference, and it is not a defect
# in the port.
#
# On SQL Server a nested procedure's SELECT flows all the way out to the client,
# so the caller's result sets include the callee's. In PostgreSQL a procedure's
# result sets are its declared INOUT refcursor parameters — a fixed list, fixed
# at definition time — so nothing surfaces unless the caller re-exports it.
#
#   CloseFiscalYear:        sqlserver returned  2 result set(s), postgres returned 1
#   RecalculateAllReturns:  sqlserver returned 18 result set(s), postgres returned 2
#
# usp_CloseFiscalYear could be made to match by giving it a second INOUT
# refcursor; usp_RecalculateAllReturns could not, because its count is
# data-dependent (one set per return processed) and no fixed parameter list can
# express that. Closing the first alone would bake arguably incidental SQL Server
# behaviour into a public PostgreSQL signature, so both are left as-is.
#
# The three procedure defects this suite originally found are all fixed and
# passing, including RunPayroll_agrees. See tests/README.md, "Known failures" and
# "The one remaining divergence: nested result sets".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DbParity.Tests.ProcedureParityTests.RecalculateAllReturns_agrees
DbParity.Tests.ProcedureParityTests.CloseFiscalYear_agrees
